_: Every divergence from the frozen spec, with the reason it exists. scripts/parity-check.mjs fails on a divergence that is not declared here AND on a declaration that no longer describes one, so this file cannot quietly become a list of things the check has stopped looking at. Keys beginning with _ are notes, not declarations. Reasons are the ones the code already carries in src/app/redesign-shell.css; this is where a reviewer reads them all at once.

_uncompared.src/app/redesign-hero.css: S2a's sheet. The only vendored spec is S1's shell.css and the S2 snapshot ships no CSS at all - its styles are inline in index.html - so there is nothing to compare this against yet. Comparing it to S1's shell reports nine divergences that are not divergences: that document is not about the hero. Freeze an S2 spec the way S1's was frozen and move this sheet into the comparison; until then this line is the record that it is NOT covered.

_spec: design/spec/S1-20260915T1938Z/shell.css, the <style> blocks of the frozen S1 snapshot the shell was transcribed from.
_clamp: The three below are one departure in three rules: the design's one-screen clamp, overridden while the views still hold pre-redesign content. Shipping it clipped the footer by 30 to 93px at ordinary laptop sizes with three links unreachable. It returns with the content designed for it, S2 to S5, enforced per slice by scripts/fit-check.mjs.
_form: Each entry names WHY it differs and WHAT we ship. The body matters: declared by selector alone, a second, different change to an already-declared rule inherits the old label - measured, an added outline on .badge .dot passed. Regenerate the bodies with PARITY_PRINT=1 node scripts/parity-check.mjs <spec> <shipped...> and keep the why.
_footer-nav: The footer nav is exactly donate, fund, terms, GitHub and jinolabs.xyz, and /limits is deliberately NOT a sixth. Read off the frozen footer rather than recalled: adding a link is a departure, and it would be departing from the design to make discoverable a page the design does not have. The refusal cards are where someone actually needs it, which is the honest argument for the placement it has. Recorded because the omission was previously nowhere, so a future reader would read an accident instead of a decision - and the ui-smoke row that asserts /limits answers 200 and names its limits is what stops it rotting to a 404 or being orphaned. If the owner wants it discoverable before a refusal, that is a design change with its own declaration, not a tidy. SDE-UI's call, 2026-09-16.

.blindfold.why: THE MASCOT'S INNER DOM IS THE `page-mascot` PACKAGE'S, NOT OURS. The design draws the fox from its own markup - .m-body, .m-head, .m-head-img, .m-tails, .blindfold inside .mascot-frame - and we render <Mascot/> from the package instead, which ships its own structure and its own styling. Transcribing these would be a second, competing description of a DOM we do not author; the first time the package changed its internals ours would be dead CSS pointing at elements that no longer exist. The visual result is checked where it can be: scripts/mascot-check.mjs measures the rendered fox in the page rather than the rules behind it.

@media (max-width:32rem) | .brand.why:
`min-width:0` ADDED (#623). The header grid could not shrink to a 320px screen: its columns measured 157.469px + 157.703px + a 10px gap = 325 inside a 292px box, so every page scrolled sideways by 19px - scrollWidth 339 against clientWidth 320, on all seven surfaces. Column one's floor is `.brand`, whose min-content is an unbreakable `white-space:nowrap` link; column two is `.hdr-right`, which cannot go below 157.7px without breaking the 44px tap floor it is already sitting on. A grid item defaults to `min-width:auto`, which refuses to shrink below min-content - the same property that pushed the footer off-screen in #610, on the other axis.

The design was drawn at widths where this never bound, so it has nothing to say about 320; this makes its header fit there rather than changing what it looks like above.

@media (max-width:32rem) | .brand .home.why: `white-space:normal` at the narrow breakpoint only (#623). This is the other half of `.brand{min-width:0}` above and neither works alone: giving the column permission to shrink does nothing while its content is one unbreakable 157.5px token. Letting "Zcash Testnet Faucet" wrap drops column one to its longest word and the page fits - scrollWidth 339 -> 320. Scoped to max-width:32rem, so the masthead is untouched at every width the design was drawn at.

@media (max-width:32rem) | .seg.why: `min-width:0`, `flex-wrap:wrap` and a tighter gap (#623). `.seg` spans both header columns, so it INHERITED the overflow above rather than causing it - it was the widest thing past the edge, which is why it reads like the cause and is not. These three are the structural guard that keeps it from becoming one: the nav may now shrink, and if a longer label or a larger font ever makes four tabs genuinely not fit on one row it wraps to two instead of escaping its parent. At the measured widths it still renders as one row, so this changes nothing visible today - it changes what happens when the content grows.

.stage .grant.why: #737, owner ask 2026-09-21T12:04Z, dated on purpose: a band across the top of every page's content, ABOVE the masthead, the first thing on the page (the owner's third look), saying the Coinholder-Directed Retroactive Grants vote is open (17 to 29 September 2026) and asking for a vote if the faucet has been useful. The snapshot has no such element; the masthead meets the hero directly. This is a DIVERGENCE, not an override: the design is still the authority, the band is up for the vote's eight days and comes out after the 29th, and while it is up everything below it - the hero included - sits lower by exactly its height, which fit-check's one-screen rule at every planned size bounds (the band gets shorter, the rule does not get looser). Built from the owner's reference (a Tailwind + motion sticky banner) with the site's own tokens: the CTA gradient and text colour, in flow rather than sticky. Its negative top margin cancels .comp's top padding so its edge is the page's, and its bottom margin makes gap plus margin equal that padding, so the masthead sits as far under the band as it sat under the page's edge. Text is #282828, not the CTA's white: white reads 2.08 to 2.85:1 on the gradient at this size and the dark reads 5.17 to 7.08:1, a literal because the gradient does not follow the theme and --ink does. The background bleeds edge to edge (owner's second look) by negative inline margins of half the gap between the stage and the content column, paid back as padding, so the words and the X stay on the column. The band costs the hero NOTHING (CTO, 2026-09-21 evening): it is exactly .comp's top padding tall (2.8u), its top margin cancels that padding and its bottom margin cancels the flex gap, so under a mouse the masthead sits on the same pixel it did without the band.
